title: Normalized Hom bijection for a transported free module sheaf
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], with $L=f^{-1}\dashv R=f_*$. Let $B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$ and $E$ a sheaf of sets there. Give $LB$ and $LM$ their ring and module operations by applying $L$ through its finite-product comparisons [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $B[E]$ be the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the sectionwise free modules $U\mapsto B(U)[E(U)]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with restrictions $\sum b_e[e]\mapsto\sum(b_e|_V)[e|_V]$ and generator $i:E\to|B[E]|$. For an $LB$-module sheaf $H$, let $R_BH$ have underlying sheaf $R|H|$ and scalar action induced by $B\to RLB$ and the direct image of the action of $H$. The module and set adjunctions induce a natural chain of bijections $$\operatorname{Hom}_{LB}(L(B[E]),H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B}(B[E],R_BH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E,R|H|)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LE,|H|).$$ The first bijection is the set-sheaf adjunction restricted to linear maps. The composite bijection is exactly $h\mapsto |h|\circ Li$, after identifying $|L(B[E])|=L|B[E]|$. In particular $L(B[E])$ with generator $Li$ represents maps from $LE$ to underlying module sheaves, naturally in $E$ and $H$.

source.place: Tag 08TQ, lemma-pullback-differentials, proof: free-module identifications; the normalized Hom-bijection justification of those identifications.

proof.text: Remove the harmless ULift wrappers from the given algebraic inverse-image presentation using explicit up/down natural isomorphisms. Construct the right module functor by the proved imageFunctor and imageFunctorUnderlying helpers of geometric module construction, applied to the right adjoint and to the adjunct of the coefficient comparison. The adjunct_binary and adjunct_constant identities show that this coefficient map preserves addition, multiplication and one. The construction gives the direct-image addition and the scalar action restricted along that coefficient map. Its product comparison equations imply precisely the addition and scalar graph clauses in the statement; restore the ULift wrappers at the end. These helpers work for the independent object and morphism universes in the statement, so no site functor is needed.

source.place: Tags 03D2 and 03D3, lemma-pullback-module and lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules: transported operations and restriction along the unit

proof.text: For an arbitrary module M, turn the addition and scalar graph clauses of its given inverse-image presentation into product-comparison equations by testing on the universal pair of projections. Use the proved binary_mate_iso_iff and linear_iff helpers of geometric module transport: under the normalized set-sheaf adjunct, commuting with addition and scalar multiplication on one side is equivalent to commuting with both operations on the other side. Their conjunction therefore restricts the underlying set Hom equivalence to linear morphisms via restrictHomEquiv. Its map equation is the original adjunct formula. Take M=B[E] and restore the lifted underlying-sheaf isomorphism to get A.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, including restriction of the underlying adjunction to linear maps

proof.text: Put $P=|B[E]|$ and omit the forgetful bars on underlying morphisms. The free-module sheaf universal property gives the second bijection, sending $\beta$ to $\beta\circ i$. The inverse of the set-adjunction bijection for $E,H$ gives the third, sending $a:E\to R|H|$ to $\varepsilon_{|H|}\circ L(a)$. Consequently the composite sends $h$ to $\varepsilon_{|H|}\circ LR(h)\circ L(\eta_P)\circ L(i)$. Naturality of the counit gives $\varepsilon_{|H|}\circ LR(h)=h\circ\varepsilon_{LP}$, and the triangle identity gives $\varepsilon_{LP}\circ L(\eta_P)=1_{LP}$. The result is exactly $h\circ L(i)$. Each arrow is bijective, so restriction to $Li$ is bijective for every $H$, as required for the asserted representing property.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof (extension from generators), and Tag 08TQ, lemma-pullback-differentials, proof (free-module comparisons); explicit adjunction normalization

proof.text: For a morphism $u:E'\to E$, the free universal property defines $B[u]:B[E']\to B[E]$ by $B[u]\circ i_{E'}=i_E\circ u$. Functoriality of $L$ and the formula from step 3 give $(h\circ L(B[u]))\circ L(i_{E'})=(h\circ L(i_E))\circ L(u)$. For an $LB$-linear $v:H\to H'$, they give $(v\circ h)\circ L(i_E)=v\circ(h\circ L(i_E))$. These equalities prove naturality of the composite in $E$ and $H$. The individual arrows are natural as well: step 2 gives module-adjunction naturality, the free universal property gives naturality of restriction to $i$, and the given set adjunction gives naturality of its inverse. Thus the displayed chain and the generator-normalized representing bijection have all the claimed naturality.
